verdict.label: Full review
verdict.summary: You can test Gmail OAuth immediately via Composio-managed apps, but bringing your own app requires creating a Google Cloud project, configuring OAuth consent, and potentially completing Google app verification depending on scopes.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail so you can start testing immediately without registering your own Google Cloud project.
whyOwnApp: You need your own app name and branding on OAuth consent screens.
You need custom scopes not covered by Composio defaults.
You need a dedicated rate limit quota instead of sharing Composio's pool.

phases.name: Create Google Cloud Project & App
steps: Go to the Google API Console to create a Google Cloud project.
Choose the Web application client type for server-side usage.
Obtain client ID and client secret.
phases.handoff: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard.

phases.name: Configure OAuth Consent & Redirects
steps: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes.
Add the redirect URI provided by the Composio dashboard.
phases.handoff: Test authentication connection via Composio session.

phases.name: Google App Verification
steps: Submit app verification request if using sensitive or restricted scopes.
Wait for Google review to remove the unverified app warning.

artefacts.title: Google Cloud OAuth Client Form Values
artefacts.body:
Application Type: Web application
Name: Your Agent App Name
Authorized redirect URI: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Scope Justification Statement for Reviewers
artefacts.body: Our AI agent application requires access to Gmail to read messages, draft responses, and send emails on behalf of the user when explicitly requested during conversational workflows.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy URL
requirements.when: Required when configuring the OAuth consent screen for public apps

requirements.label: Security Assessment / External Audit
requirements.when: Required if your public application stores restricted scope data on servers or transmits it

scopes.purpose: View your email messages and settings.
Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.
View your email message metadata such as labels and headers, but not the email body.

redirectRules.rule: Register the exact redirect URI provided by the Composio dashboard in the Google API Console.

blockers.cause: The OAuth client ID was not found or is incorrect in your request.
blockers.fix: Double-check your Client ID in the Google API Console and update your integration configuration.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio-managed app configuration which handles client credentials automatically.

checklist.text: Determine if you want to use the Composio-managed Gmail app or create a custom app.
Create a Google Cloud project in the Google API Console.
Configure the OAuth consent screen with correct app branding and privacy policy links.
Select required Gmail scopes (e.g., readonly, modify, send).
Add the Composio redirect URI to your Google Cloud project credentials.
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard auth config.
Submit for Google verification if utilizing sensitive or restricted scopes for public distribution.

uncertainties: Exact verification turnaround times by Google Trust and Safety are variable and not strictly bounded by documentation.
Specific volume limits for refresh tokens per user-client combination are not exhaustively quantified in public docs.

claims.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail so you do not need to register your own OAuth app initially.
You should use your own OAuth app when your product's branding requirements call for your app name on OAuth consent screens.
claims.quote: You need your app name on OAuth consent screens. Use your own OAuth app when your product's branding requirements call for it.

claims.text: You should use your own OAuth app when you need custom scopes not provided by Composio defaults.
claims.quote: You need custom scopes. Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).

claims.text: You should use your own OAuth app when you are hitting rate limits because managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
claims.quote: You're hitting rate limits. Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.

claims.text: To begin obtaining OAuth 2.0 client credentials, visit the Google API Console.
claims.quote: Visit the Google API Console to obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials such as a client ID and client secret that are known to both Google

claims.text: For server-side or JavaScript web apps use the Web application application type.
claims.quote: For server-side or JavaScript web apps use the Web application application type. Don't use this application type for any other application

claims.text: Obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from the Google API Console.

claims.text: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes to define what information is displayed to users and app reviewers.

claims.text: If your public application uses scopes that permit access to certain user data, it must complete a verification process.
claims.quote: If your public application uses scopes that permit access to certain user data, it must complete a verification process.

claims.quote: Sensitive : These scopes provide access to specific Google user data that users authorize for your app. They require additional OAuth App Verification.
